metadata.title: Ancient, eclipsing, tidally-locked: A blue lurker progenitor in the population of extreme-velocity star candidates

evidence.quote: In this letter, we report the identification of the candidate HVS Gaia DR3 4265540383431508736 (J1903-0023 from here on), as a tidally synchronised binary in the halo.
In this letter, we report the identification of the candidate HVS Gaia DR3 4265540383431508736 (J1903-0023 from here on), as a tidally synchronised binary in the halo.
J1903-0023, one of the brightest targets, stands out as high priority candidate for follow-up spectroscopy using the X-shooter instrument at ESO-VLT.
making it one of the closest known HVS candidate.

evidence.quote: we get a \gamma = -130 \pm 40 km s^{-1} with a slightly inflated uncertainty

notes: J1903-0023: selected as a known high-priority HVS candidate (T:p1-b15) and followed up spectroscopically (T:p1-b7); although the authors explicitly conclude it is bound to the Galaxy (T:p4-b2, T:p5-b2), the follow_up category applies regardless of the current boundness conclusion, so it is not treated as candidates_found. J0725-2351: analysed as the extreme-velocity sdF comparison star (T:p1-b13), not identified as a Galactic unbound candidate; its rest-frame velocity is revised downward to 240 km s^{-1} (T:p4-b3), so no eligible contribution category applies.

Gaia DR3 4265540383431508736: No right ascension, declination, or proper-motion components are explicitly reported for J1903-0023, and no numerical bound/unbound probability or total Galactic-rest-frame speed is given for it; the Toomre-diagram U, V, W components are not converted to a total speed here. The paper reports two slightly different spectroscopic distances for J1903-0023: 1.46 ± 0.1 kpc in Table 3 (T:p3-b9) and 1.45 ± 0.1 kpc in the text (T:p3-b11); both are retained. The Gaia DR3 parallax is 0.40 ± 0.06 mas (T:p1-b15), while the earlier DR2 value is 0.19 mas (T:p3-b11). The X-shooter, NOT, and SOAR RVs are individual measurements of the radial-velocity-variable binary, whereas gamma = -130 ± 40 km/s is the systemic value.
